chunks: Al-Husayn b. Ahmad (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: My father narrated to us. He said: Ibrahim b. Hashim narrated to us from al-Husayn b. Yazid al-Nawfali from Isma'il b. Abi Ziyad al-Sakuni from al-Sadiq Ja'far b. Muhammad from his father from his forefathers from Ali (peace be upon them). He said:

Seize the opportunity to supplicate at five occasions: (1) during the recitation of the Quran, (2) during the adhan, (3) when rain falls, (4) when two rows meet for martyrdom, and (5) at the supplication of the oppressed, for it has no barrier beneath the Throne.

key_terms.الدعاء: supplication (du'a) - calling upon Allah with requests and devotion
key_terms.الشهادة: martyrdom - dying for the sake of faith
key_terms.الغيث: rain - in Islamic tradition, rain is a sign of divine mercy
key_terms.المظلوم: the oppressed one - whose supplication is never rejected
key_terms.حجاب: barrier/veil - obstruction between the supplication and the Throne

ai.seo_question: What are the five best times for supplication according to Imam Ali?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Amali of Shaykh al-Saduq, Imam Ali (AS) identifies five occasions when supplication is most readily accepted by Allah: during Quran recitation, at the adhan, when rain falls, when armies meet for battle, and at the cry of the oppressed. The teaching emphasizes that the du'a of the oppressed ascends directly to the Throne of Allah without any barrier, highlighting the gravity of oppression in Islamic ethics.
